subject: Clarify pricing: ingestion vs seat-based for observability add-ons
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@archival.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify pricing: ingestion vs seat-based for observability add-ons

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the demo last week. We chatted internally about Archival's expected ingestion profile and wanted to confirm how you'd prefer us to frame the observability add-ons in the commercial:

- Do you want pricing modeled as an ingestion-slab (GB/day or TB/month) plus trace storage, or as a seat-linked observability SKU (per-seat + small ingestion buffer)?
- Is predictability (flat month-to-month cost) more valuable for you than potentially lower unit cost with a usage model?

If you can share rough ranges for concurrent users and daily ingest (I attached the CSV you sent — I trimmed a column), we can build two neat options:

A) Ingestion-slab centric: price by ingestion tiers, tracing billed by retention window and query QPS, dashboards priced per seat or per dashboard pack.
B) Seat-anchored: annual per-seat fee that includes X MB/day ingestion and Y months of trace retention; overages billed at a blended rate.

Quick ask: which of the two framing would your procurement team prefer as the starting point? If neither, tell us the procurement levers and we'll adapt.

I'll loop in Kim and Marcus on pricing math once you confirm.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: archival-observability-usage.csv (CSV stub, trimmed), demo-recording-link.txt
From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@archival.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Archival Procurement <procure@archival.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify pricing: ingestion vs seat-based for observability add-ons

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick follow. Procurement prefers predictability, but our finance lead also wants to avoid a large premium for low-util months. High level:

- Typical ingest today: 750 GB/day peak, average ~220 GB/day. Expect growth to ~1.2 TB/day within 9 months as we onboard new lines.
- Concurrent seats: 35 power users, but only ~10 heavy dashboard users who run ad-hoc traces.
- Retention: we need 90 days of full trace retention for compliance in one business unit; others can be 30 days.

Procurement note (cc): If we lock an annual commitment, what kind of true-up/attrition protection do you offer? Also any discounts for multi-year commits?

Thanks — attaching the latest export and procurement checklist.

—Alyssa
VP Product
Archival AI

Attachments: archival-latest-export.csv (CSV stub), procurement-checklist.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify pricing: ingestion vs seat-based for observability add-ons

Folks —

I ran a quick model based on Alyssa's numbers. Two clean options to present:

1) Predictable Slab Plan (ingestion-first)
   - Commitment: 1TB/day slab (covers peak with buffer) + seat pack for dashboards (25 seats)
   - Trace retention: 90 days for BU1 (billed as premium retention policy), 30 days for others
   - Discount: 18% off list on the combined package for a 12-month commitment; true-ups at quarter-end if commit exceeded.

2) Seat-Pivot Plan (seat-first)
   - Commitment: 35 seats annual commitment; includes 250 GB/day ingestion allowance + 30-day retention by default.
   - Add-on: extra ingestion consumed at $0.XX/GB (blended rate); 90-day retention add-on per BU at $Y/month per seat affected.
   - Discount: 12% on seats for 12-month, 20% for 24-month.

Notes/asks:
- Marcus: confirm blended overage rate for ingestion and the true-up cadence.
- Jordan: do we want to offer a one-time onboarding credit to offset first-month spike? Sales often uses a one-time 10% usage credit.

I'll compile a two-column commercial and short SOW blurb.

Kimberly
Director, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-scenarios-v2.pdf (pricing matrix + SOW blurb)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@archival.ai>, Archival Procurement <procure@archival.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify pricing: ingestion vs seat-based for observability add-ons

Alyssa / Procurement —

Thanks for the data and notes. Based on internal alignment (see Kim's options below) we propose the following as a starting point for negotiation:

- Offer: Predictable Slab Plan (recommended)
  - 1TB/day committed ingestion slab to start, quarterly true-ups, 18% package discount for 12 months.
  - 25 dashboard seats included; additional dashboard seats at list less 12% volume discount.
  - 90-day retention for the compliance BU at a premium retention rate (we'll itemize in the SOW).
  - One-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of first-month billed ingestion to smooth your initial spike.

If you prefer the Seat-Pivot Plan, we can present that with a 12% initial seat discount or 20% for a 24-month commit; ingestion overages will be the blended $0.045/GB rate (Marcus confirms).

Next steps:
1) Let us know which plan you want as the base (Slab vs Seat).
2) If Slab, procurement: confirm the desired true-up cadence (quarterly vs monthly) and any legal constraints on multi-year discounts.
3) I will send a short commercial summary + SOW and a DocuSign link for the initial MSA amendment (if needed).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the numbers.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
